name: Mayhaw

facts.where: Wet bottomlands and swamp edges of East Texas

caution: Eat the flesh; the small seeds are not chewed. Never eat a wild plant on this guide's word alone. Confirm identity against several sources and learn the look-alikes first.

sections.title: Harvesting
sections.body: Mayhaws drop into the water and shallows below the tree; traditional gatherers float them out with nets. A wet-footed harvest with a devoted following.

sections.title: In the kitchen
sections.body: Mayhaw jelly is a genuine Southern delicacy, tart and bright pink, and the whole reason anyone learns this tree.
